newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Australia diamond stocks turn dull.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Australia diamond stocks turn dull.

text.p: A lack of new discoveries is turning investors off to Australian diamond exploration stocks, according to David Russell, mining analyst for Perth brokerage Saw James Capel Ltd.

Australian investors have largely been weaned on companies involved in straight-forward gold exploration, where the chances of success are higer than in diamonds, Russell said in an interview at the close of the Paydirt diamond conference here.
As a result, the diamond exploration stocks are seen to be the "absolute most speculative end of the speculative exploration industry," Russell said.
The average share price for 14 diamond explorers surveyed by Capel have declined by just over 35 percent in the last two years, Russell said.
"The market capitalisation of most of the smaller companies are at such a level that they are not deemed attractive to institutions," he said.
"They are actually at a level now where they are living hand to mouth," he said.
Russell said institutions should be looking at a "development capital market-type of portfolio" given that just one or two institutions were currently backing diamond exploration in Australia.
Market fundamentals for diamonds are improving and should lead to a balanced market by 1998, Russell said.
The analyst said he was recommending a portfolio of Australian diamond companies, most of which have either joint venture or marketing arrangements with South African miners.
These include Auridiam Consolidated NL, Striker Resources NL and Moonstone Diamonds Corp NL. Each company has some interests outside of Australia.
Exploration in Australia, he said, has not delivered.
The success rate among diamond explorers runs at only about 0.3 percent compared with 40 percent for gold exploration, Russell said.
As a result, most funding comes from highly speculative investors, he said.
Unfortunately for local diamond explorers, this has not translated into more interest by foreign investors, who might otherwise regard the companies as a good buy, he said.
The likely source of venture capital would be Canada, where investors are acccustomed to investing in more speculative resource stocks, Russell said.
But the Canadians have their own diamond plays to invest in, he said.
"This makes it very difficult for Australian explorers to excite Canadians to come over," Russell said.
Increasingly, Australian explorers are listing on Canadian exchanges to tap directly into their markets, Russell said.
They also are diversifying operations into more tried and true activities, such as gold exploration, in order to add a "bit of sex appeal," Russell said.
"Pure diamond exploration just isn't attracting the interest anymore," he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
